title: Orifice Plate

introduction.definition: An orifice plate flowmeter is a plate with a precise sharp-edged hole clamped between flanges. The restriction accelerates the flow and lowers its static pressure; a DP transmitter measures the pressure difference across the plate, and flow is calculated from the square root of ΔP (ISO 5167-2). It is simple, inexpensive and standardised, but causes a high permanent pressure loss.
key_points: Sharp edge and straight runs govern accuracy
Permanent loss ~40–90 % of ΔP depending on β
introduction.summary: An orifice plate flowmeter is a thin plate with a precise sharp-edged hole clamped between two flanges. The restriction speeds the flow up and lowers its pressure; the pressure difference between upstream and downstream taps is measured by a DP transmitter, and the flow rate is proportional to the square root of that difference (ISO 5167-2). Simple, cheap and standardised, but with a high permanent pressure loss.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: ΔP rises with flow²; flow computed as q = K·√ΔP.

pressure.title: Pressure profile
pressure.description: Static pressure is highest just upstream of the plate, lowest at the vena contracta just downstream (where the jet is narrowest and fastest), then partly recovers. The unrecovered part is the permanent pressure loss (relatively high for orifice plates). Flow ∝ √ΔP (ISO 5167-2).

foundation: Support the meter run; avoid vibration at the transmitter.
alignment: Centre the element precisely in the pipe bore (eccentricity affects accuracy).
piping: Provide straight upstream/downstream lengths per ISO 5167 for the fittings present, or use a flow conditioner.
Slope impulse lines: liquids — transmitter below taps; gas — transmitter above taps.
commissioning: Fill/vent impulse lines; zero the transmitter with the equalising valve.
Check the flow computation (β, density, units).

video_tutorials.title: Orifice Plate — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Orifice Plate.
An orifice plate flowmeter is a plate with a precise sharp-edged hole clamped between flanges.

The restriction accelerates the flow and lowers its static pressure; a DP transmitter measures the pressure difference across the plate, and flow is calculated from the square root of ΔP (ISO 5167-2).
It is simple, inexpensive and standardised, but causes a high permanent pressure loss.
Typical applications include process flow measurement (liquids, gases, steam); natural gas metering (AGA 3); pump minimum-flow detection; restriction orifices (pressure reduction).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Orifice Flanges with Tap Holes, Gaskets & Bolting.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Orifice Plate works.
Flow approaches the plate with a developed velocity profile.
The bore forces the flow to contract and accelerate.
Pressure is lowest at the vena contracta just downstream.
Taps in the orifice flanges transmit p1 and p2 to the DP transmitter.
Downstream, pressure partly recovers; the rest is permanent loss.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Static pressure is highest just upstream of the plate, lowest at the vena contracta just downstream (where the jet is narrowest and fastest), then partly recovers.

video_tutorials.title: Orifice Plate — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Orifice Plate.
Check transmitter zero.
Pull and inspect plate edge and flatness.
Replace plate if edge is rounded or plate bowed.
Watch for reading low: under-reads. Common cause: rounded/worn edge, plate installed backwards.
Watch for erratic reading: noisy δp. Common cause: gas in liquid impulse lines, swirl.
Watch for deposits: drift. Common cause: fouling upstream face.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
